Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage is dominated by the violent unwinding of the AI trade following Anthropic's record-breaking IPO, with major outlets converging on how the Claude maker's wild trading debut helped tip the S&P 500 and Nasdaq into correction territory amid a broader $4 trillion tech wipeout. Secondary threads include fallout from Nvidia's leadership crisis and a new SEC probe, Trump's threatened tax on offshore AI data centers, and marquee interviews from the NYT's DealBook Summit.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO Turmoil Caps $4 Trillion AI Wipeout on Wall Street
stories.summary: Anthropic's stock gave back nearly all its first-day gains within two sessions of its record IPO, a slide Wall Street now blames for accelerating a broader AI-driven selloff that pushed the S&P 500, Dow and Nasdaq into correction territory and wiped out the Nasdaq's 2026 gains. Fortune reported Anthropic priced at $83, popped 17% on debut, then fell about 9-11% the next day as chipmakers Nvidia and AMD dropped more than 13%, while Axios noted the Nasdaq plunged 5.3% and the S&P fell into correction.

stories.headline: Nvidia Faces US Regulator's Probe Into Its Accounting
stories.summary: The SEC has opened an investigation into Nvidia's accounting, compounding the chipmaker's troubles following Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO amid a scandal; Forbes reported Nvidia fell further Friday, with Huang having lost nearly $48 billion, or almost 30% of his net worth, since the affair surfaced.

stories.headline: Trump Threatens 'Tremendous' Tax on Data Centres Built Outside US
stories.summary: President Trump floated a steep tax on American firms building AI data centers abroad, framing it as a move to keep the US ahead of China in the AI race; the BBC noted Trump gave little detail, with aides reportedly caught off guard by the proposal.

stories.headline: Elon Musk on His Politics, a Potential Merger and Ukraine
stories.summary: Tesla and SpaceX chief Elon Musk discussed his political views, a potential corporate merger and his take on Ukraine in a wide-ranging interview at the DealBook Summit, one of several marquee conversations from the event that also featured Satya Nadella and Zohran Mamdani.

stories.headline: Citi Undercounted $35 Billion in Assets at U.K. Subsidiary
stories.summary: Citigroup disclosed a record-keeping error that undercounted $35 billion in risk-weighted assets at a U.K. subsidiary, a fresh setback for CEO Jane Fraser's push to shore up the bank's internal controls.

stories.headline: Judge Approves $7 Billion Settlement Over Claims That Roundup Caused Cancer
stories.summary: A federal judge approved a $7 billion nationwide class-action settlement over claims that Bayer's Roundup weedkiller caused non-Hodgkin lymphoma, a deal expected to resolve tens of thousands of pending lawsuits.

stories.headline: Europe's Power Market Is Flashing a Warning to Its Economy
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that soaring electricity costs are already forcing manufacturers to curb output, pointing to a German steel plant where it is sometimes too expensive to keep producing, a sign of strain in Europe's industrial base.

stories.headline: China Military Bars SF Express Over Procurement Misconduct
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that Chinese logistics giant SF Express has been suspended from military-wide procurement of goods and services over alleged violations, a blow to one of China's largest delivery companies.

Business.gaps: Puck and Politico had no business/markets coverage in the feed or search results relevant to this topic; Business Insider was not found via search and had no feed items provided.

US politics.overview: Coverage is dominated by the fallout from Trump's Asia trip and his Shenzhen summit with Xi and Putin, a frantic lame-duck Congress trying to pass permitting reform and salvage a reconciliation package before Democrats take over in January, and a sharp stock market selloff tied to AI-bubble fears. Outlets are also heavily focused on both parties' early 2028 positioning in the wake of Democrats' sweeping 2026 midterm wins.

stories.headline: Trump touts Asia trip and Xi/Putin summit but offers little in results
stories.summary: Trump held a White House press conference calling his Asia trip one of the best in history, but reporters noted the trilateral summit with Xi and Putin produced little beyond a joint statement, with Trump also threatening penalties on firms that build AI data centers abroad.

stories.headline: U.S. stocks slide into correction territory amid AI and tech worries
stories.summary: Markets posted their worst week since last year's tariff-driven selloff as fears over an AI bubble hit tech stocks and dragged the Nasdaq into the red for the year.

stories.headline: Senate passes sweeping permitting overhaul, sends it to the House
stories.summary: After a standoff with progressive Democrats delayed a quick vote, the Senate passed a bipartisan permitting reform bill meant to speed up energy infrastructure, with a final House vote expected after Thanksgiving.

stories.headline: Senate GOP's third reconciliation push collapsing in final weeks of majority
stories.summary: House Republicans say the Senate's defense-heavy $350 billion reconciliation package is dead on arrival without spending offsets, a blow to Trump with just over two weeks left before Democrats take control of Congress.

stories.headline: Trump threatens 'tremendous penalties' on firms building data centers abroad
stories.summary: At a wide-ranging press conference, Trump said he would tax or block U.S. tech companies from building AI data centers overseas, framing it as a way to keep jobs and investment at home and block China from benefiting.

stories.headline: Democrats coalesce around Medicare expansion plan for next Congress
stories.summary: Democrats are rallying around expanding Medicare coverage once they control Congress in January, though senators are still debating whether to add dental/vision/hearing benefits, lower the eligibility age, or both, and how to pay for it.

stories.headline: Both parties scramble to define their 2028 strategy after the midterm wipeout
stories.summary: Incoming NRSC chair Bernie Moreno calls the GOP's 2028 Senate map 'brutal' after losing the majority, while Democratic governors and officials debate who should lead the party's next presidential ticket and how to keep the coalition that just delivered a landslide.

stories.headline: Hakeem Jeffries nears history as first Black House speaker
stories.summary: As Hakeem Jeffries prepares to become the first African American speaker of the House, commentators are examining his rise and how he'll navigate a newly empowered but ideologically split Democratic caucus.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS's search results returned mostly older stories (weeks to months old); nothing from the outlet could be confirmed as published in the last 24-48 hours. Politico, NYT, WSJ and The Guardian coverage is limited to the feed items provided since these outlets block direct search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage overnight is dominated by the fallout from Anthropic's blockbuster but turbulent Nasdaq debut, which coincided with a brutal AI-stock selloff that outlets are calling the worst week for tech since the pandemic. Secondary threads include Trump's threat to tax US firms building AI data centers overseas, a contested AI-generated proof of the Riemann hypothesis, mounting Nvidia regulatory scrutiny, and a wave of stories on AI-driven cybersecurity and privacy risks.

stories.headline: Anthropic's turbulent IPO debut deepens a $4 trillion AI stock wipeout
stories.summary: Anthropic's shares gave up most of their first-day gains and briefly traded just cents above the IPO price, capping a brutal week in which the Nasdaq fell into a bear market amid deepening doubts about AI spending; Platformer separately reported the company raised $81.3 billion in the largest-ever IPO, valuing it at $1.76 trillion at close.

stories.headline: Trump threatens 'tremendous' tax on companies building AI data centers abroad
stories.summary: President Trump said he would impose a "tremendous tax" on US tech firms that build AI data centers outside the country, framing it as a fight to keep Beijing from leading in AI even as some states move to restrict domestic data center growth.

stories.headline: Dueling claims over a 167-year-old math problem: AI proof vs. human proof
stories.summary: An Anthropic mathematician says he used Claude to produce a formalized proof of the Riemann hypothesis, only for Stanford researchers to release a competing all-human draft hours later, sparking debate among mathematicians over which (if either) holds up.

stories.headline: Nvidia faces SEC accounting probe and California subpoena over chip exports to China
stories.summary: The SEC is investigating Nvidia's accounting practices following Jensen Huang's resignation, while California's attorney general has separately subpoenaed Nvidia to determine whether its chip exports ended up in China in violation of export controls.

stories.headline: YouTube reportedly set to pay $3 billion to settle school districts' addiction claims
stories.summary: YouTube is said to be preparing a $3 billion settlement with thousands of school districts that sued over claims its "addictive design" harmed children, according to Bloomberg reporting cited by the outlet.

stories.headline: Signal blocks screenshots on iOS and Android to stop AI agents from reading private chats
stories.summary: Signal is disabling screenshot capture to prevent AI agents such as Apple's Siri, Google's Gemini and Meta's Muse from reading private conversations, calling the agents an "existential threat" to messaging privacy.

stories.headline: AI is hollowing out China's job market faster than elsewhere, Bloomberg data shows
stories.summary: A Bloomberg analysis of 10 million job postings found AI-exposed roles in China are disappearing roughly 10 percentage points faster than less-exposed roles, with entry-level and creative workers hit hardest as Beijing races to reshape industrial policy around AI.

Tech & AI.gaps: Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, The Economist, The Guardian, IEEE Spectrum, Google DeepMind and OpenAI did not have newsworthy AI/tech items beyond what's cited above in the last 24-48 hours; for outlets that block search (Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, The Guardian) only items from the provided feed were used.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are converging on the COP31 talks in Antalya, where a draft deal drops calls to phase out fossil fuels, alongside mounting worries about grid reliability and affordability as AI data centers strain US and European power systems. US permitting reform legislation and Europe's strained industrial power market are also drawing heavy coverage.

stories.headline: COP31 negotiators drop fossil-fuel phase-out language as deal nears
stories.summary: Negotiators at the UN climate talks in Antalya, Turkey dropped calls to accelerate a fossil fuel phase-out while moving toward a deal endorsing electrification of the global economy, with a draft text offering compromises on climate finance and trade curbs. Separately, the EU's climate chief called a new US-Russia-China deal to expand fuel production and supply an "unfortunate reality," warning against falling into another energy "trap."

stories.headline: US permitting reform bill advances to House amid Democratic divisions
stories.summary: A permitting reform bill cleared the Senate and heads to the House, but Democrats remain split over provisions some see as troubling changes to environmental law and state and tribal authority, while others argue no better deal is available.

stories.headline: Europe's power market is flashing a warning to its economy
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that at a German factory there are increasingly hours when producing steel is simply too expensive, illustrating how volatile power prices are squeezing European industry.

stories.headline: Grid operators brace for winter reliability risks as data centers strain the system
stories.summary: FERC's winter market assessment found improved coordination in the West should help offset low hydropower output from a drought-hit Colorado River basin, while New England risks over-relying on oil this winter; separately, Latitude Media reported that NERC found just three US regions face "elevated" blackout risk this winter as batteries and gas help buffer the grid.

stories.headline: PJM urged to delay capacity auction over data center demand forecasts
stories.summary: State ratepayer advocates and PJM's own market monitor are urging the grid operator to delay its December capacity auction until data center demand is stripped from forecasts, warning that proceeding as planned threatens reliability and could cost consumers billions.

stories.headline: A shipwreck becomes new ammunition in the fight against offshore wind
stories.summary: Heatmap reports that opponents of a Rhode Island offshore wind farm are using a 2019 shipwreck that claimed two lives as new ammunition against the project, after the group Green Oceans asked federal regulators to investigate whether the wind farm hindered the rescue.

stories.headline: Russia says cargo ship attacked by drones in Gulf of Finland
stories.summary: Russia said a cargo ship bound for its Kaliningrad exclave was targeted by drones in neutral waters, a strike Bloomberg says highlights growing risks to the country's energy and food exports.

stories.headline: Hyperscale data centers now consume power on par with a mid-size country
stories.summary: A new study reported by Latitude Media found that hyperscale data centers now use nearly as much electricity as the state of Michigan, with more than half of that power coming from fossil fuels and the sector's US emissions rivaling Denmark's.

Energy.gaps: Canary Media's and E&E News's most recent available articles via search were more than a week old, so no current (last 24-48h) stories could be confirmed for them. Argus Media could not be checked due to search limits. Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT and The Economist block web search and had no relevant feed items provided, so their current energy/climate coverage could not be assessed.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage is dominated by the historic Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral summit in Shenzhen and its diplomatic fallout, alongside intensifying US-China tech decoupling (chip export curbs, Alibaba and Tencent AI announcements) and market turmoil in Taiwan tied to a global AI stock rout. Business outlets are also tracking Chinese corporate and EV-sector moves, while state media frame the summit as a historic diplomatic win for Beijing.

stories.headline: Xi hosts historic first-ever trilateral summit with Trump and Putin in Shenzhen
stories.summary: State-run Xinhua reports that Xi chaired the first-ever face-to-face meeting of Chinese, Russian and US heads of state, which produced a joint declaration on nuclear risk reduction, UN reform and energy security; Trump separately called it one of the most momentous summits in years. State-run Global Times and CGTN echoed the framing of the meeting as groundbreaking, while SCMP, Nikkei Asia, Caixin Global and Hong Kong Free Press covered the event and its aftermath, including Trump defending the summit amid domestic backlash.

stories.headline: US pushes new rules to keep top Nvidia AI chips from China, but gaps remain
stories.summary: The Wire China reports the Trump administration is finally restricting Chinese access to advanced Nvidia chips, though experts say the new rules still leave important loopholes; related coverage flagged a Beijing-based server vendor, Intelliture, that sold to a blacklisted Chinese university despite Nvidia courting it as a client.

stories.headline: China's military bars SF Express from procurement over alleged misconduct
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that logistics giant SF Express has been suspended from military-wide procurement of goods, engineering and services over alleged violations, a notable blow to one of China's top delivery firms.

stories.headline: China's industrial output growth slows sharply in October, missing forecasts
stories.summary: Caixin reports that China's value-added industrial output grew 4.8% year-on-year in October, a slowdown from September that missed economists' forecast of 5.3%, with auto manufacturing and raw materials weighing on activity even as electronics and export deliveries stayed strong.

stories.headline: Taiwan stocks plunge nearly 28% from October peak as AI rout deepens, prompting emergency stabilization steps
stories.summary: Focus Taiwan reports the Taiex fell over 6% Friday to its lowest close in nearly seven months, down roughly 28% from its October 6 record high amid global AI-sector concerns, prompting the premier to order stabilization measures and the market regulator to tighten short-selling rules.

stories.headline: Alibaba trains next-generation Qwen model on its own in-house chips
stories.summary: TechNode reports Alibaba is using chips from its semiconductor unit T-Head to train its next Qwen model, a move CEO Eddie Wu disclosed on the company's earnings call as Beijing pushes chip self-reliance amid tighter US export curbs.

stories.headline: Tencent releases open-weight Hy4 flagship AI model with million-token context
stories.summary: TechNode reports Tencent released downloadable weights for its flagship Hy4 AI model, following its initial launch earlier in November, as Chinese tech firms race to match Western AI labs on open-source releases.

stories.headline: CATL and Hesai added to Hong Kong's Hang Seng Tech Index in major expansion
stories.summary: CnEVPost reports the Hang Seng Tech Index is expanding to 50 constituents effective December 7, adding battery giant CATL and lidar maker Hesai, while self-driving firm Momenta joins the broader Hang Seng Composite Index.

China.gaps: Could not find recent China-beat coverage from Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, China Daily, CGTN (beyond summit framing), or Yicai Global in this window.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by the deepening US-Israel-Iran conflict and its regional spillover, with Houthi missile strikes on Riyadh's financial district, drone and tanker incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and renewed Gaza violence all drawing heavy coverage. Alongside the security crisis, Gulf business outlets are tracking a parallel story of resilient economic momentum, with sovereign wealth funds deepening Wall Street partnerships and Moody's forecasting continued Gulf growth despite regional instability.

stories.headline: Houthi missile strike damages Riyadh's tallest tower, PIF headquarters
stories.summary: A Houthi missile attack damaged several floors of the 80-story Public Investment Fund Tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, with Saudi authorities reporting no injuries but condemning what they called a terrorist act; the Saudi-led coalition responded with a major military operation against Houthi targets and continued intercepting missiles and drones through the weekend.

stories.headline: Iran says it still wants diplomacy as Trump calls Tehran's terms unacceptable
stories.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi said Tehran still hopes diplomacy can end its war with Washington, while President Trump said Iran wants a deal but has not offered terms he can accept, leaving the conflict unresolved as Vice President Vance declined to say whether he'd have ordered strikes on Iran.

stories.headline: Iran claims downing of US drones, tanker set ablaze near Strait of Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps said it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone over the Strait of Hormuz using a newly developed air defence system, claiming the 58th aircraft destroyed since the war began, as separate reports described a tanker catching fire after hitting a mine and two tankers hit by projectiles near Oman's Khasab.

stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill Palestinians in Gaza as Board of Peace adviser criticises Israel
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed nine people in Gaza, drawing criticism from a Board of Peace adviser, while separate reporting detailed Israeli quadcopters dropping explosive-laden boxes on Palestinian families in Gaza.

stories.headline: UAE's Nusseibeh hits setback in UN secretary-general race
stories.summary: Former UAE UN ambassador Lana Nusseibeh's bid to become the next UN secretary-general suffered a setback after the UK, France and China voted against her in a Security Council straw poll, even as she had jumped to third place among candidates, leaving the race deadlocked.

stories.headline: Cop31 climate talks run into overtime amid dispute over final deal
stories.summary: Negotiations at the Cop31 climate summit extended past schedule as delegates remained divided over the terms of a final agreement.

stories.headline: Wall Street deepens partnerships with Gulf sovereign wealth funds
stories.summary: Major US asset managers are shifting from courting Gulf sovereign funds to becoming partners, exemplified by Apollo's deal to acquire a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, which is expected to support Mubadala's global expansion and deepen Apollo's Gulf ties; Blackstone separately opened a new Dubai wealth-management office building on its Abu Dhabi presence.

stories.headline: UAE growth seen staying resilient despite regional tensions, Moody's says
stories.summary: Moody's said the UAE should remain one of the Gulf's more resilient economies as government spending and diversification support non-oil growth, even as the agency warned Gulf countries remain exposed to disruptions from Strait of Hormuz tensions, while forecasting Saudi Arabia's growth to rebound sharply from a 2026 contraction to over 5% in 2027.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Haaretz, Ynetnews, Al Arabiya English (beyond the shared Houthi story), Zawya and Asharq Al-Awsat yielded no additional distinct leading stories beyond those already cited; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, BBC and The Economist could not be searched directly and are reflected only via the provided feed items.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: African-focused outlets are dominated by the renewed Ethiopia-Eritrea military standoff around Badme and South Africa's post-election coalition maneuvering, alongside geopolitical shifts following the UN's Western Sahara exit and signs of political strain in Uganda. Business and fintech coverage highlights surging African instant payments, mining royalty changes in Côte d'Ivoire, and Nigerian corporate news, while Africa Confidential and The Africa Report also track security and succession stories across the Sahel, DRC and Somalia.

stories.headline: Ethiopia-Eritrea tensions flare again over Badme
stories.summary: Eritrean troops have retaken the border town of Badme amid reported drone strikes and artillery bombardments, with Ethiopian and Eritrean forces now within striking distance of each other and fears growing of a full-scale repeat of their 1998-2000 war.

stories.headline: ANC deal keeps DA out of Johannesburg, blocking Zille
stories.summary: A political deal between the ANC and ActionSA appears set to exclude the Democratic Alliance's Helen Zille from the Johannesburg mayoralty despite her party topping the vote, deepening South Africa's fractured post-election coalition politics.

stories.headline: UN exit from Western Sahara hands Morocco a strategic prize
stories.summary: Africa Confidential reports that the winding-down of the UN mission in Western Sahara (Minurso) is giving Morocco new leverage in its decades-long dispute with Algeria over the territory, reshaping North Africa's security map.

stories.headline: African instant payments hit $1.8 trillion as transactions triple
stories.summary: A new AfricaNenda-led report finds African instant payment systems processed 71.4 billion transactions worth $1.8 trillion in 2025, nearly triple 2021 levels, though a trust deficit still pushes many users toward cash.

stories.headline: Côte d'Ivoire to raise mining royalties ahead of IMF talks
stories.summary: Côte d'Ivoire plans to raise the royalty rates mining companies pay in order to boost government revenue ahead of possible talks with the IMF on a new financing programme.

stories.headline: Wagner's gold interests complicate Central African Republic peace talks
stories.summary: Negotiations between Bangui and N'Djamena over the return of exiled Central African Republic rebel leaders sheltering in Chad are being complicated by entrenched Wagner-linked gold mining interests.

stories.headline: Former South African deputy president and UN Women chief dies at 71
stories.summary: Phumzile Mlambo-Ngcuka, who served as South Africa's first female deputy president and later headed UN Women from 2013 to 2021, has died at 71.

Africa.gaps: The Continent had no recent items surfaced in the feed or search; Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT and WSJ block search and had no relevant Africa items in the provided feed, so their current coverage could not be assessed.

Media.overview: Media-trade coverage over the past day is dominated by renewed turmoil at CBS News, where a fresh round of Skydance-driven buyouts hit staff including the London bureau and some 60 Minutes producers, alongside continuing fallout from the Telegraph's leadership shake-up. Trade outlets are also tracking the fight over public broadcasting funding, union healthcare pushes in Hollywood, and new industry debates over AI deals and newsroom ethics.

stories.headline: CBS News staffers take Skydance buyout offers as cost-cutting continues
stories.summary: Dozens of CBS News employees, with the London bureau and some 60 Minutes staff among the hardest hit, accepted buyout offers this week as Skydance pushes for $6 billion in savings following its Warner Bros. Discovery purchase, though the total represented less than 10% of those offered the package.

stories.headline: Robert Winnett leaves Telegraph for Daily Mail amid wider UK job cuts
stories.summary: Press Gazette reports that longtime Telegraph deputy editor Robert Winnett is departing after 19 years to join the Daily Mail, part of a broader wave of UK journalism layoffs the outlet is tracking, including People Inc cutting 195 jobs and roughly 100 cuts at the Telegraph.

stories.headline: SAG-AFTRA launches healthcare lobbying group and approves Netflix contract
stories.summary: SAG-AFTRA's board created a new task force to lobby for more affordable member healthcare plans while separately approving a 2026 Netflix contract that includes an estimated $33 million in increased residuals.

stories.headline: Public media funding is returning, but is it time for a deeper rethink?
stories.summary: Nieman Lab examines how federal funding for public media is set to resume roughly 318 days after the Corporation for Public Broadcasting formally ceased operations, prompting debate over whether the system needs a structural overhaul rather than a simple restoration.

stories.headline: Milwaukee Journal Sentinel faces lawsuit over thinly sourced story
stories.summary: CJR reports that the Journal Sentinel published a thinly sourced article raising allegations against a candidate's conduct with women, prompting a lawsuit after he responded with a serious counter-accusation against the paper.

stories.headline: Semafor discloses paid ties to Trump and Harris-aligned operatives
stories.summary: Mediaite reports that Semafor updated 11 articles and newsletters to disclose financial relationships with political operatives, including Trump adviser Jason Miller and a former Harris aide.

stories.headline: Politico bets on AI workflow tools to monetize its journalism
stories.summary: Puck's Dylan Byers reports that Politico has integrated its data and journalism directly into Claude and ChatGPT via a new product, with product chief Francesca Barber betting robust journalism can command a premium akin to a 'Claude-ified Bloomberg Terminal' as publishers grapple with collapsing search traffic.

stories.headline: Willie Geist departs MS NOW to focus on NBC News full-time
stories.summary: Adweek reports Willie Geist is leaving MS NOW to commit fully to NBC News, while Skydance CEO David Ellison reiterated that CBS News and CNN will continue operating as separate units.

Media.gaps: NYT, WSJ, and FT block web search and had no relevant feed items provided. The Guardian's only feed item was an unrelated general-news story (Trump/datacenters), so no media-industry item was available from it.
